Subject: Root cause & mitigation: keepalive semantic change in proxy layer

Team — final RCA and customer-facing summary. Posting here so Naomi can share with ProcureCorp.

Summary: a config change in our proxy (kept at canary until 11:00 on 2026-07-15) changed the keepalive probe behavior to send fewer zero-length heartbeats under idle conditions. Under high-throughput bursts this increased the window where a client-side library (some ProcureCorp SDK versions) would classify the stream as stalled and initiate a reconnect. Reconnects during ongoing chunked transfers produced partial-chunk delivery and client-side timeouts. The regressions were visible across ~0.5-3% of streaming sessions depending on burst intensity.

Mitigations applied: 
- Immediate: rolled proxy config back at 10:58 on 2026-07-15 (already done).
- Short term: pushed a runtime patch to aggressively flush pending chunk buffers and made SO_KEEPALIVE probes more aggressive (deployed 2026-07-15 10:58).
- Medium term: added a runtime guard to always send periodic non-empty keepalive delimiters when chunked streams are active; will ship in 2 weeks (2026-07-31).
- Long term: add QA e2e tests that simulate client SKD behavior under bursty throughput and a canary metric that tracks partial-chunk rates across regions.

Customer action items: Naomi to send an executive-facing summary and a 2-week ETA for the medium-term fix. Offer a good-faith credit for the impacted billing window if ProcureCorp requests it.

Attachments: stream-trace-20260717.log (aggregated traces), partial-chunk-example.txt

Markus
